title: Measuring Application Performance
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of measuring application performance in a jQuery application.
Apply browser performance tools in a small example and describe its expected result.
Verify network panels with an explicit test or browser observation.
status_note: Draft generated from the attached syllabus and official references; requires lesson-by-lesson technical review, local execution, accessibility checks, and editorial approval.

content.intro: Use this lesson on measuring application performance as a professional review habit: identify the relevant behavior, make one controlled change, and verify its outcome.
content.why_it_matters: This topic is useful because it turns browser performance tools into a repeatable implementation choice. Measure before optimizing. Cache repeated selections, batch DOM updates, delegate events when appropriate, cancel stale requests, and avoid unnecessary layout reads or animation work.

content_blocks.run_instructions: Use a local HTML page with jQuery 4.0.0 loaded before app.js for JavaScript snippets. HTML and package-manager snippets can be checked as configuration examples. Run the interaction in browser DevTools, inspect the DOM/Network panel, and compare actual behavior with the expected result. Do not submit learner code to the production API for arbitrary execution.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the original markup and code, clear console/network filters, reload the local page, and repeat the same interaction. For a request example, return the mock endpoint to its original response before retrying.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Start with a known DOM structure, apply the pattern for measuring application performance, and test one normal case plus one edge case. Keep selectors scoped to the intended component and verify the real browser result.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Measure a small interaction before and after an improvement related to measuring application performance. Record the test setup and avoid claiming a gain without comparable measurements.

task_acceptance_criteria: The implementation demonstrates measuring application performance using a current, documented approach.
The learner records the expected and actual behavior and checks at least one edge case.
The example preserves semantic HTML and does not render untrusted data as HTML.
The test setup and any runtime limitation are documented honestly.
hints: First identify which DOM nodes and runtime state are involved in measuring application performance.
Make one small change, inspect the resulting element or request, and compare it with the expected result.
If the result differs, check the selector, script order, browser console, event target, and relevant API documentation before adding more code.
content.expected_output: Records a simple timing sample. Use repeatable browser Performance recordings before concluding that an optimization helped.
common_mistakes: Assuming a selector matched an element without checking the collection length.
Confusing jQuery collections with native DOM elements or live properties with markup attributes.
Using .html() with untrusted data or assuming client-side validation enforces server rules.
Treating a demo snippet as production-ready without testing failure and accessibility states.
summary: Measuring Application Performance is one part of the performance and optimization workflow.
Measure before optimizing. Cache repeated selections, batch DOM updates, delegate events when appropriate, cancel stale requests, and avoid unnecessary layout reads or animation work.
Use the official API or upgrade guide for version-specific behavior and verify an example locally before relying on it.
